reason.text: The repo scope grants full access to public and private repositories, including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks, as well as management of organization-owned resources and user-owned projects.
reason.label: sourced

sources.quote: | repo | Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks. Note: In addition to repository related resources, the repo scope also grants access to manage organization-owned resources including projects, invitations, team memberships and webhooks. This scope also grants the ability to manage projects owned by users. |

reason.text: The repo:status scope grants read and write access to commit statuses in public and private repositories, without granting access to the code.
reason.label: sourced

sources.quote: | repo:status | Grants read/write access to commit statuses in public and private repositories. This scope is only necessary to grant other users or services access to private repository commit statuses without granting access to the code. |

reason.text: The repo_deployment scope grants access to deployment statuses for public and private repositories, without granting access to the code.

reason.text: The public_repo scope limits access to public repositories, including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository projects, collaborators, and deployment statuses for public repositories and organizations, and is also required for starring public repositories.
reason.label: sourced

sources.quote: | public_repo | Limits access to public repositories. That includes read/write access to code, commit statuses, repository projects, collaborators, and deployment statuses for public repositories and organizations. Also required for starring public repositories. |

symptom.text: Organization members cannot authorize an OAuth app to access organization resources without owner approval when access restrictions are enabled.
symptom.label: sourced

sources.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators must request approval from an organization owner before they can authorize an OAuth app that has access to the organization's resources.

cause.text: OAuth app access restrictions are enabled for the organization, requiring owner approval for app authorization.
